cohort: 128 individuals undergoing cesarean delivery (56 pre-implementation and 72 post-implementation of ERAS pathway)
finding: The implementation of an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery pathway for all cesarean deliveries decreased both inpatient and outpatient postpartum opioid use without increasing pain scores or decreasing patient satisfaction.
mod_finding: This study examined the effect of an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway for all cesarean deliveries on postoperative pain and found that it reduced opioid use without negatively impacting pain scores or patient satisfaction.
